children: 1624 ET - U.S. natural gas futures settle lower with the December contract retreating from the $3 level in its debut at the front of the curve. Near-term weather forecasts remain warmer than usual, pointing to weak heating demand for the first part of November. The EIA reported an 80 Bcf storage build for last week, which was bigger than to 70 Bcf estimate in a WSJ survey of analysts, and slightly above the 77 Bcf five-year average for the week. "Prices were already pushing lower this morning prior to the storage report, and the bearish nature of the data did little to alter that trajectory," Andy Huenefeld of Pinebrook Energy Advisors says in a note. "If current weather forecasts hold, we could see at least four additional builds before the scales tip to net withdrawals." Nymex natural gas settles down 2.6% at $2.952/mmBtu. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

1545 ET - Treasury yields fall after both the Fed and the ECB keep interest rates unchanged, while U.S. indicators show growth and inflation still hot. Futures markets price in hikes in December, according to LSEG. Third-quarter employment costs in the U.S. are expected to cool down slightly, according to a WSJ consensus. October Chicago Business PMI is forecast to decline to 56 from 58.8. The 10-year falls 0.056 percentage point to 4.988%, snapping a four-day rising streak. The two-year falls 0.077 point to 4.654%, down for two consecutive days. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1358 ET - Microsoft deserves credit for engineering efficiency gains that allowed it to increase its cloud computing capacity without more incremental costs in F1Q, StoneX analyst Yi Fu Lee says in a note. But the company is also experiencing delays in third-party capacity deliveries, he says, meaning the cloud business is not fully de-risked. "Engineering can only bridge a physical capacity gap for so long," Lee says. "Microsoft has demonstrated that engineering can unlock underutilized CPU and GPU capacity, but sustaining near-50% Azure growth will eventually require delayed physical infrastructure to arrive and enter production." Microsoft is off 1% at $525.68.(elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1358 ET - Microsoft's new Agents and Infra segment, part of the company's September revamp of its reporting segments, demonstrates the flexibility of the company's approach to cloud computing capacity, StoneX analyst Yi Fu Lee writes. "We are impressed by how Microsoft increasingly manages AI infrastructure capacity like an investment portfolio, allocating a scarce and fungible asset toward the highest-return opportunities while considering strategic tradeoffs," Lee writes. The new segment, which spans Microsoft's full AI stack, "acknowledges that the economic return on AI infrastructure should not be evaluated solely through the margin of any one product," he adds. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1337 ET - For shares of Google parent Alphabet to be re-rated going into 2027, the company will need to innovate on its search business and release and scale agentic AI offerings, Morgan Stanley analysts say in a note. They compare the stock to Meta, which has successfully released a consumer AI agent while maintaining advertising growth well above Google's Search growth. Google's plan to release its own Gemini-based consumer AI agent this year is a start, but the Meta comparison creates a high bar for Alphabet, the analysts say. "Not to say that they can't clear it (and should given their leading tech, data and distribution) but they need to in order to regain incremental investor confidence," they say. Alphabet tumbles 12% to $284.83.  (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1330 ET - Though Microsoft's F1Q print was headlined by an acceleration in Azure cloud growth, there are other important positive trends under the hood, Morgan Stanley analysts say in a note. "The acceleration in growth continues to come with strong underlying economics," they say, noting that gross margins of 67.8% beat estimates by 60 basis points, and that operating margins were around 50% despite high AI investments. "With growth accelerating, AI monetization broadening, and infrastructure efficiencies supporting operating leverage, we view the Q1 print as another clear validation of our thesis that Microsoft's AI investments can drive durable high-teens revenue growth and >20% earnings growth," they say. Microsoft is off 1.1%. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1300 ET - ServiceNow's outlook has investors worried, but its underlying business is still promising, according to Oppenheimer in a note. ServiceNow's stock plunged 25% after the company beat expectations by a narrower margin than before and implied a slowdown in 4Q cRPO [current remaining performance obligations], analysts Brian Schwartz and Idan Gutkind say. These elements leave concerns about organic growth durability, they say. ServiceNow's AI momentum hasn't established a clear path to speeding up organic growth, according to the analysts. However, they believe the stock is worth buying because ServiceNow has an expanding opportunity with AI and a differentiated growth profile. (katherine.hamilton@wsj.com)

1248 ET - ServiceNow's latest results didn't convince investors that it's building momentum, JPMorgan analysts say. Investors are primarily concerned about a projected slowdown in the company's cRPO [current remaining performance obligations] metric, the analysts say. The slowdown is largely due to ServiceNow changing the scope of the cRPO metric to remove certain revenue drivers, the analysts say. The analysts think cRPO will eventually recover, as there are signs of strength in the underlying business. ServiceNow tumbles 25%.(katherine.hamilton@wsj.com)

1232 ET - Google's Search slowdown in the third quarter is a navigable problem, but it could weigh on shares at least through the fourth quarter, JPMorgan analysts write in a note, lowering their price target by $50 to $375. The monetization headwinds in AI Mode could respark concerns of an AI Search air pocket, the analysts write. "Search also faces tough comps & bigger FX headwinds in 4Q, & AI Mode monetization may take some time to kick in," they write. "This could keep pressure on Google shares near-term, or make them range-bound." Shares of Google parent Alphabet drop 12% to $282.57. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1228 ET - The likelihood of a recession striking in the next 12 month sits at about 10%, based on the latest economic data, Glenmede's Michael Reynolds says in a note. It's an unusual read on an economy that's in its sixth year of expansion, he says. But there are reasons to believe some of the economic weakness seen in 2022 and 2023 helped reset the economy's underpinnings, even if a formal recession didn't happen, Reynolds says. This is a function of how durable U.S. growth has proven against a long list of shocks, including this year's surge in energy prices, he says. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

1226 ET - The deceleration in Google's 3Q search revenue raises questions about the company's monetization of AI Mode and AI Overview, UBS analysts write in a note, lowering their price target to $332 from $380. "Google struck what was a more measured/deliberate tone around monetization of incremental AI queries, which to us suggests a lower ad revenue growth trendline than we had anticipated," the analysts write, adding that the company took a "measured approach to monetization" even prior to AI. The third-quarter search showing compares unfavorably to Meta Platforms' revenue growth, the analysts add, noting that a Meta AI search product may be intensifying competition risk. Shares in Google parent Alphabet fall 12% to $282.76. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1225 ET - D.R. Horton says its fiscal 2027 guidance has "wider ranges than usual" citing continued uncertainty across the broader economy. "We expect affordability constraints, higher mortgage rates and cautious consumer sentiment to continue to pressure new home demand," SVP of Communications Jessica Hansen says on a call with analysts. For the year, the homebuilder currently expects revenue of $30 billion to $32 billion, missing Wall Street estimates. (connor.hart@wsj.com)
